conviction_note: The period is half pre-released: the 16 Sep AGM update said trading was in line and the FY guide unchanged. The move therefore sits on lines nobody has seen yet: whether the Gateway submarine-support contract is signed before the bridge ends on 30 Nov, a possible further Type 31 provision at the new CEO's first results, H1 cash, and the CEO's promised update. abs_move is 5.0 (UK base 3-7, raised for a new CEO, a contract decision due inside the month and 37.5% realised vol in a weak defence tape); p_up is 48 because the small positive and small negatives roughly cancel. Findings sum -0.3 against a scaled -0.2; the two agree.

findings.finding: The FMSP bridge was extended for only two months from 1 Oct 2026, so it runs out at about the end of November. The HY27 release (19 Nov) is the last scheduled communication before then and must give the Gateway Agreement's status. A signing or a firm completion date removes the sole-provider nuclear-support overhang; a third extension would read as slippage.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bridging news was released as standalone RNSs (Apr 2026 six-month bridge, 30 Sep two-month extension); the next session's move was not measured for either. The CEO said on 16 Sep that the bridge has 'enabled us to continue to deliver increasing levels' of support.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether the release carries a signing is unknown. No press report of a signing was found by 18 Nov, and the share price has fallen 9.8% over 60 days, with no rally pricing in a signed deal. If a signing were expected, the stock would have held up better than peers into the print; instead it fell with them (QinetiQ, Chemring and BAE in the same week).
findings.independence: The company's own AGM statement (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/babcock-international-group--bab/agm-trading-update/9773929) says the Gateway agreement 'is finalised'; that is a second Babcock document, not an independent source.

findings.finding: Babcock's Marine CEO is quoted (via Navy Lookout, 2 Nov) that HMS Venturer's handover has slipped to 2028, about two years late, with cumulative Type 31 losses above £300m and acceleration 'difficult without additional investment'. At a new CEO's first results this raises the risk of a further provision or a reset in commercial terms beyond June's £140m charge.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26 final results with the £140m Type 31 charge: -5.89% on 22 Jun 2026 (baseline history), the largest reaction in the sample.
findings.original_quote: Babcock's total losses under the Type 31 frigate construction contract have exceeded £300 million. Meanwhile, the company's management notes that accelerating construction under the program's current funding arrangements will be difficult without additional investment.
findings.why_not_priced: The slip is public, but whether the June charge already covered a two-year delay is not, and the company has not updated its estimate since 22 Jun. Sized small because it may well be covered already: the £140m was booked for rectification, and the Marine CEO's own figure may be the basis of that charge. If the market expected a new charge, the 5-day drawdown would be name-specific; instead it tracks the defence sector.
findings.independence: UKDJ, 6 Feb 2026 (https://ukdefencejournal.org.uk/language-on-timeline-for-new-type-31-frigates-shifts/): the MOD moved Venturer to 'in service and ready for operations by the end of this decade', away from a 2027 date. Same direction, earlier.

findings.finding: QinetiQ, the closest UK MOD-services peer, said on 12 Nov that 'customer funding and procurement delays continue to affect the near-term top line growth'. Babcock's own 16 Sep update flagged that the MOD is still confirming how the Defence Investment Plan will be implemented, which is a small top-line risk to Babcock's UK Land and Marine lines in H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Babcock fell 4.29% on 12 Nov 2026, QinetiQ's results day, with QinetiQ -4.4% (Yahoo daily closes), so the read-across was traded the same day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Babcock fell 4.3% the same day. What is left is small, and Babcock's revenue sits mostly on long-term contracts (about 70% under contract at 1 Apr, per FY26 results), which caps the transmission.
findings.independence: Babcock AGM update, 16 Sep (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/babcock-international-group--bab/agm-trading-update/9773929): 'in the near term the UK Government continues to confirm the details of the implementation of their Defence Investment Plan'.

lessons_applied: 'Too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 4.5 to 5.0 for a half-pre-released period with a new CEO and a contract decision due within the month
'A finding about a number already told is worth 0' and 'narrow proxy / macro transmission': the QinetiQ read-across cut from -0.3 to -0.2, since it was traded the same day
'Your own caveat has to reach the number': the Type 31 finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6, because June's charge may already cover the public two-year slip
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': H1 cash flow named as a line in new_in_release; no sized finding, since there is no evidence on it
